title: Fenwick Pay POC - Compact Infosec Bundle and Annotated Q&A
content:
Purpose and scope:
This is a compact, annotated bundle prepared for the Fenwick Pay POC (Nov 2025). It combines: (a) our curated answers to the customer's security questionnaire, (b) workshop notes from the technical run-through on 2025-11-06, and (c) a short evidence index pointing to artifacts we can hand to Fenwick for their audit team.

High-level summary (consumer friendly):
- Redwood hosted API for the trial (no private deployment requested for POC).
- Data flow: customer -> TLS-terminated Redwood edge (regional) -> tenant-scoped inference pool (isolated VPC). No customer data is persisted beyond configured retention and KV cache TTL for the POC.
- Primary controls demonstrated: TLS 1.2+/mutual TLS option, KMS-backed envelope encryption, SOC2 attestation (latest report excerpt), periodic vulnerability scanning, role-based access controls with MFA.

Workshop / runbook notes (2025-11-06):
- Attendees: Priya (SE), Evan (Infra), Marisol (SRE), Fenwick infra lead (Jordan F.), Fenwick security (A. N. Parker).
- Demo flow: API key issuance -> region pinning -> sample chat with PII redaction toggle -> automated KV-prefix cache enabled -> load profile simulation (30 tps, 128 token avg).
- Observations: KV cache TTL defaulted to 5m; for POC we recommended 1h to reduce cost and show caching benefits. Fenwick asked for clear deletion path for cached entries (action item).
- Risk note from Fenwick: must demonstrate KMS key separation for dev vs prod. We showed customer-managed key option; Fenwick asked for steps to rotate and re-encrypt existing cached prefixes (open).

Annotated Q&A (short answers with evidence pointers):
1) Data classification and handling (Q: Do you store customer prompts or derived outputs?)
   Answer: By default Redwood does not retain prompts beyond configured logging/retention windows. For hosted POC we set retention to 7 days. Customers can opt out of telemetry.
   Evidence: logs-retention-policy-2025-10.pdf (CONF-SEC-2025-07), sample-telemetry-config.json (github PR 4278).

2) Encryption at rest and in transit
   Answer: TLS 1.2+ for all in-flight traffic; server certificates rotated via automated CA pipeline. Data at rest uses AES-256-GCM envelope encryption; root keys are stored in KMS (AWS KMS or customer-provided external KMS via BYOK HSM connector).
   Evidence: kms-rotation-policy-2025.txt; byok-connector-arch.png (linked in CONF page).

3) Key management and rotation
   Answer: Automated rotation every 90 days for service-managed keys; customers can bring their own keys (BYOK) and control rotation via their KMS. Re-encryption flows tested on staging but full rewrap in-prod is run-booked (work in progress for fenwick POC).
   Evidence: runbook-kms-rotate-2025.md (linked to JIRA SEC-1123).

4) Access controls and identity
   Answer: RBAC across console/API, SSO via SAML/OIDC, mandatory MFA for privileged roles. Service accounts scoped per-tenant with least privilege.
   Evidence: iam-policies-snapshot-2025.csv; sso-config-sample.txt.

5) Logging, monitoring, and retention
   Answer: Audit logs captured for control plane actions; request traces for inference calls retained for debugging (default 7 days). Logs are immutable and exported to customer-designated sink on request.
   Evidence: sample-audit-log.json (sanitized); monitoring-alert-rules.yaml.

6) Incident response and vulnerability management
   Answer: IR playbook exists; we run quarterly pen tests and weekly automated SCA + vulnerability scans. For critical vulnerabilities we notify customers within 24 hours of triage.
   Evidence: ir-playbook-excerpt.txt; pentest-summary-2025-Q2.pdf.

7) Third party dependencies and supply chain
   Answer: We maintain an SBOM for runtime libs and 3rd-party services used in hosting. Major infra components have CVE tracking.
   Evidence: sbom-runtime-2025.csv (artifact).

8) Compliance attestations
   Answer: SOC2 Type II report (most recent) available under NDA; ISO scope in progress. Fenwick asked for a short excerpt showing control mapping to data retention and encryption controls.
   Evidence: soc2-excerpt-nondisclosable.pdf (delivery via secure share once NDA confirmed).

Evidence index (compact):
- logs-retention-policy-2025.pdf (CONF-SEC-2025-07)
- kms-rotation-policy-2025.txt (CONF-SEC-2025-07)
- runbook-kms-rotate-2025.md (JIRA SEC-1123)
- sample-audit-log.json (sanitized log snippet included below)
- pentest-summary-2025-q2.pdf (internal pentest vendor)
- iam-policies-snapshot-2025.csv
- sbom-runtime-2025.csv
- monitoring-alert-rules.yaml
- telemetry-optout-process.txt

Sanitized audit log snippet (for demonstration only):
2025-11-06T14:03:22Z | tenant=f-wk-pay | actor=service-account:ingress-proxy | action=generate-token | request_id=7a1f-... | result=200
2025-11-06T14:03:24Z | tenant=f-wk-pay | actor=redwood-api | action=inference.request | model=redwood-7b-open | tokens_in=34 | tokens_out=89 | duration_ms=92

Open items and action owners (POC timeline):
- A1: Provide step-by-step re-encryption flow for BYOK rotation and confirm compatibility with KV-prefix cache. Owner: Evan Lee. Due: 2025-11-12. (status: in progress)
- A2: Provide short excerpt of SOC2 mapping that references encryption and logs (deliverable under existing NDA). Owner: Linh Nguyen. Due: 2025-11-10. (status: awaiting legal clearance)
- A3: Add explicit cache deletion API example to docs and demo script. Owner: Priya Raman. Due: 2025-11-14. (status: done - demo updated)
- A4: Confirm support for mutual TLS for inbound Fenwick calls (they use strict mTLS in prod). Owner: Marisol Ortega. Due: 2025-11-09. (status: validated on staging)

Customer-specific notes and concessions:
- Fenwick requires tenant key separation between dev and prod and an audit trail showing rewrap events. We confirmed separation and a rewrap audit-event (example included in sample-audit-log above) but need to produce a concise rewrap report for them.
- Fenwick asked for default telemetry to be off; for the POC we set telemetry=off and explicit opt-in.

Risks and mitigations: 
- Risk: POC uses hosted multi-tenant pools; Fenwick sensitivity suggests eventual move to Dedicated pools for production. Mitigation: present Dedicated diagram and cost delta in next workshop.
- Risk: BYOK rotation + cached prefixes could lead to stale cache keys after rewrap. Mitigation: runbook includes cache invalidation step post-rotation; we will simulate in staging and capture results.

Appendix: quick links to artifacts (internal):
- Confluence: CONF-SEC-2025-07 (Fenwick POC workspace)
- Jira: SEC-1123 (KMS rotation runbook), SE-778 (POC demo tasks)
- PR: github.com/redwood-inference/pr/4278 (telemetry opt-out sample)
- Slack thread: security-fenwick-thread (high-level questions and final sign-off message)

Notes to self (informal):
- Capture a short screencast of the cache deletion API call (helps procurement/security validators).
- Double-check that pentest summary redactions don't remove required CVE references.
- If Fenwick insists on HSM-backed BYOK we should prepare a short estimator for Dedicated with HSM attachment.

End of compact bundle. This doc is intentionally concise for the Fenwick audit team; full evidence artifacts live in CONF-SEC-2025-07 and JIRA SEC-1123.

Last updated: 2025-11-18 by Priya Raman (draft).
